explain.say: Did you know almost every country on Earth has made a promise to you? It is the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, from 1989. A convention is a written agreement between countries. Look at the board: its promises sorted into four boxes.

faq.q: What is the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
faq.a: It is an agreement adopted by the United Nations on 20 November 1989. Its 54 articles list the rights every child under 18 should have, and governments that ratify it promise to protect them.

faq.q: Do children really have a right to play?
faq.a: Yes. Article 31 says every child has the right to rest, play and leisure, and to join in cultural and artistic life.

faq.q: What should I do if someone hurts me?
faq.a: Tell a grown-up you trust, like a parent, teacher or school counsellor. Many countries have free child helplines, such as 1098 in India or Childline on 0800 1111 in the UK.
asks: Who can I tell if I am not safe?

faq.a: Article 12 says children can give their views on matters that affect them, and adults should take those views seriously, depending on the child's age and maturity.
asks: Do adults have to listen to children?

faq.q: Why has the USA not ratified the convention?
faq.a: The USA signed it in 1995 but has not ratified it. Some Americans worry it could affect parents' rights or state laws; others want the country to join. It still has many child protection laws of its own.
asks: Which country has not signed the UNCRC?

facts: The UN adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child on 20 November 1989; it has 54 articles.
Every UN member state except the United States has ratified the Convention.
